amanda_cs: FYI onboarding convo with Embark Inc — they hit a mix of 401s then sustained 429s after we provisioned their service account. Can someone help triage? customer says errors start ~30s after first warmup requests.
leo_eng: thanks — can you paste a minimal failing request? 401 then 429 usually points to token reuse / ephemeral TTL mismatch or preflight fanout.
amanda_cs: main snippet from their serverless warmup: 
```
POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral_token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model":"rwdllm-3b",
  "input":"hello"
}
```
They rotate tokens every 45s in their infra. After the first 10 warmup invocations everything goes into 429s for a minute.
maria_se: quick hypothesis: their warmup fanout creates a thundering herd of preflight/auth calls that exceed per-key concurrency window. If tokens rotate too fast we get brief 401s while backend falls back to rate limiting.
leo_eng: agree. Two-prong fix: 1) add jitter + exponential backoff on 401s during provisioning so clients don't immediately retry all requests; 2) cache ephemeral tokens per-worker for at least 60s to avoid rotation overlap. Also set max concurrency on their SDK pool — try maxConcurrency=6 as a start.
amanda_cs: noted. They use our JS-lite SDK default config. Any quick config snippet I can share?
maria_se: share this patch to their init: 
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  tokenProvider: rotateToken,
  maxConcurrency: 6,
  authRetry: { attempts: 3, baseDelayMs: 200, jitter: true }
});
// ensure rotateToken caches token for 60s per worker
```
leo_eng: Also check their token provider header — if they occasionally send `Authorization` missing scope or empty string we return 401 then the backlog triggers 429s. Ask them to log request headers for the failing timeframe.
amanda_cs: they attached a short log excerpt — shows intermittent `401 Authorization missing` and then a flood of `429 quota_exceeded`.
sre-bot: metric alert: embarksandbox.prod key (client_id: emb-1234) spiked in 5m 429 rate from 2% -> 47% at 3309991065. Top route: /v1/embedding (warmup path).
leo_eng: good data. If they can't change warmup pattern quickly, we can mitigate on our side: temporarily bump their per-key soft concurrency cap and enable a 30s grace on token rotations for that key while we steer them. I'll need approval from ops.
amanda_cs: noted — customer prefers self-serve changes first. I'll send the SDK patch. If they still see >25% 429 after 15m we'll ask ops for a grace window.
tim_pm: flagging renewal risk — Embark is in POC and spends heavily on latency tests. If onboarding stalls >3 days we should escalate to account executive. Can we get a timeline?
amanda_cs: proposing: SDK patch + call today 1600 PT, re-evaluate 15m after patch. If still bad, request ops grace. I’ll update AE.
maria_se: also recommend they run a simple preflight coalescer in front of warmup that debounces identical warmup calls for 1s — trivial change for serverless.
leo_eng: steps for the call: 1) confirm token TTL and per-worker caching, 2) apply SDK config, 3) share header logs, 4) if needed we apply temporary cap tweak.
amanda_cs: thanks team — I'll post the SDK snippet to the customer and schedule the call. Action items: Amanda -> share patch + call link; Leo -> ops escalation note drafted if needed; Maria -> quick doc blurb on warmup debounce.
